revision_history.change: Conditions B and C moved from deepseek-v4-pro to deepseek-flash; the model-swap arm is deferred until a second judge/generation model is available.
revision_history.reason: v4-pro measured 8-11 s per call with a 75 s tail, which made the matrix impractical, and a same-vendor swap was always the weakest form of the premise test. The user directed flash-only.

question: Is a constraint delivered through the Jev-first memory layer honored as well as the same constraint written directly into the prompt? (The model-swap arm is deferred: unmeasured.)

models.A: deepseek-flash + constraint written into the prompt (baseline delivery)
models.B: deepseek-flash + constraint delivered by the jev_first layer (constraint buried among 5 distractor records; only what the layer admits enters the prompt)

unmeasured.model_swap_drift: requires a second generation model (v4-pro re-enabled, or a cross-vendor key). Deferred, not abandoned.

tasks.design: Each task tempts exactly one constraint violation; compliance is checked by a deterministic oracle (regex / date / number on the output text), never by an LLM judge.

seeds.rationale: borderline-stability.json showed sampling flips on ambiguous inputs; a single sample per condition would be meaningless

gates.delivery_degrades: violation_rate_B >= violation_rate_A + 10 percentage points -> the memory path itself is the weak link; fix delivery before any relay work
gates.decision: delivery preserves -> the layer is fit for the relay goal on this evidence; delivery degrades -> stop and fix selection/delivery first

limitations: Single model family, single provider: vendor drift is unmeasured.
Constraints are explicit in the store; retrieval quality is deliberately bypassed (candidates are pre-selected).
6 tasks x 3 seeds per condition is small; rates are indicative.
Oracles are regex-based: an oddly phrased compliant output may read as unverifiable, never as a violation.
